newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest businessman shot four times, survives.
newsitem.headline: Budapest businessman shot four times, survives.

text.p: A Hungarian businessman was shot four times outside his home late on Wednesday in the latest in a rash of shootings and violent incidents in Budapest.

Police said the businessman, identified only by his initials, had been shot in the chest, arms and hands with a gun equipped with a silencer in front of his garage in a residential district. He was expected to survive.
"We have just begun investigating the crime scene," Andras Rozsa, National Police spokesman, told Reuters.
Police made no immediate link with recent bombings and shootings which authorities have blamed on a gangland turf war in the Hungarian capital.
Jozsef Prisztas, a well-known figure of the Budapest underworld, was shot dead on November 1 at point-blank range. A prominent racehorse owner was seriously wounded two weeks later.
Several hand grenades have been exploded during the last three months outside night clubs, injuring no one, but causing extensive damage in some cases.
National and Budapest police have recently beefed up the task force working on the cases to 160 officers from the previous 130, but have not yet put an end to the violence.
